event: Elsie wakes in the attic room to bread-smell and lake mist on the round window.

memory.fact: The Honeycomb's attic is one narrow room with a sloped ceiling and a round window over the canal.

pictured.coverAfter: The room was a narrow strip under the roof, the round window

event: She greets her four potted plants by name, then washes at the cold basin.

memory.fact: Elsie's plants are Mrs Pennywhistle the fern, Sunny the lemon, Doris the aloe and Captain the mint.
Elsie has small soft breasts with pale pink nipples, and a little rose-pink hair over her pussy.

pictured.coverAfter: She said good morning to her four plants by name, and watered Captain the mint twice.

event: She laces her novice's cream halter, hands unsteady, and clips the flower above one ear.

changes.note: Novice adventurer's outfit put on: slot → body
Flower clip worn above one ear: slot → head

memory.fact: Elsie wears a cropped cream halter top laced up the front, a short sage-green skirt and tall boots.
Elsie's soft rose-pink hair is a short layered bob with side-swept bangs and a pink-and-white clip.

pictured.coverAfter: The novice's outfit lay folded on the stool. The cream halter
pictured.outfit: cropped cream halter top laced up the front, short sage-green skirt, brown belt with pouches, fingerless leather gloves, tall boots, healer's satchel, pink-and-white flower clip above the left ear

event: She seals the week's letter, counts her coins, and packs the satchel: salve, bandages.

changes.note: She counts her coins: purse shown to the player

memory.fact: Elsie writes her mother a letter every week.
Elsie's mother, Hana Fairweather, still travels the southern caravan roads.
Coin is copper pips, silver lanterns and gold suns: ten pips a lantern, twenty lanterns a sun.

event: Elsie eats a warm roll at the bakery, and the baker waves her out.

memory.fact: The Honeycomb is a bakery on Thimble Canal, kept by a small, round-faced widow in her sixties.

pictured.coverAfter: Downstairs the baker put a warm roll in her hand before she could get a word out.

event: She posts the letter at the corner shop; two women go by arm in arm.

memory.fact: Two women together are ordinary in Lanternmere, and nobody looks twice at them.

event: The Hall of Naming stands white above the lake, its glass dome full of morning.

memory.fact: The Hall of Naming is a white stone hall with a glass dome, on the lakeshore.
Lanternmere is a guild city of canals and arched bridges on the shore of a wide lake, the Mere.

pictured.coverAfter: The Hall of Naming stood at the end of the lakeshore road, white stone

event: The girl ahead asks if she is nervous; Elsie says yes, and warms her cold hands.
Inside, a priestess calls the names; the first girl's window opens above her.

memory.fact: A priestess of the Hall calls each name, and each steps alone into a silver circle in the floor.
The System's window opens in the air above the circle, and the whole hall can read it.

event: Elsie hopes for simples; then her turn comes, and she steps into the circle.
It reads: Enthraller.

changes.note: Class: Enthraller, read in the Hall's window

memory.fact: Elsie Fairweather's class is Enthraller.

event: She reads it twice; the silence spreads outward and nobody in the hall moves.

memory.fact: Lanternmere still whispers of Vesper Locke and the War of Strings at the word Enthraller.

event: A woman in the gallery rises and walks out; the priestess calls no next name.
Elsie says, Oh! that sounds like a lot of responsibility, and steps down.
The hall does not clap; outside, the others from the line look at her and away.
She walks down from the hall alone, and the city is warm and ordinary around her.
The guild hall is timber and noise, its green copper roof across Brightwater Square.

memory.fact: The guild hall is a great timber hall with a green copper roof on Brightwater Square.

pictured.coverAfter: The guild hall stood across Brightwater Square under a green copper roof

event: In the registration line, the clerk takes her name and asks her class.
She says Enthraller; the clerk's pen stops, and he goes up the stairs.
The guildmaster comes down, grey and sword-calloused, and takes Elsie up.

memory.fact: The guildmaster is a grey-haired retired A-rank swordswoman in her fifties, with an office upstairs.

event: She reads the Strings Accord: every skill reported, none on anyone unwilling.

memory.fact: Under the Strings Accord every Enthraller is registered with the guild and watched by a Warden.
An Enthraller's Warden writes down every skill she uses and reports it to the guildmaster.
Under the Accord an Enthraller may use a skill on no one who has not agreed, unless it saves a life.

event: Told the watching is so nothing goes wrong, Elsie says she is glad of it.
She counts the fee onto the desk; the clerk stamps a copper tag with an F.

changes.note: Guild registration fee, two lanterns: 134 → 114 pips
Purse logged at 114 pips after the guild fee
F-rank: the clerk stamps an F on her copper tag

memory.fact: Registering costs two lanterns, and each adventurer gets a copper rank tag stamped with her name.

event: The guildmaster opens the charcoal door: a young woman stands with a black ledger.

memory.fact: Cora carries a black leather ledger and writes everything down in a small, exact hand.

pictured.coverAfter: Then the guildmaster opened a door painted charcoal, and beyond it stood
pictured.outfit: charcoal guild coat buttoned to the throat with the silver Warden pin, dark trousers, black boots, black leather ledger

event: Warden Corisande Vane, called Cora, will go with her and write down every skill.

memory.fact: The Warden Corisande Vane is called Cora.
Elsie Fairweather's class is Enthraller.
An Enthraller's Warden goes with her on all guild business, dungeons included.

event: Cora will report each to the guildmaster; Elsie thanks her for coming.
Cora does not answer; Elsie asks what she likes in her tea.
Cora says: black and strong, one sugar; Elsie says she will remember it.

memory.fact: Cora drinks her tea black and strong with one sugar, and nobody has ever asked how she takes it.

event: Back in the hall, Elsie reads the F-rank notices, then finds the party board.

memory.fact: The quest board runs the length of the hall, its notices sorted by rank from F up to S.
The party board is where parties chalk their names on slates and seek adventurers to fill them.
On the F-rank board today: moonbells from the Glasswood's edge for an apothecary, six lanterns.
On the F-rank board today: cellar rats under the Crooked Kettle tea house, four lanterns.
On the F-rank board today: a lost goat somewhere in the Underbloom's first floor, three lanterns.

event: Parties look each other over and nobody looks at her; the slates she asks are full.
The fourth slate is turned to the wall; the cast-offs' slates stand at the corner.
A woman with a great axe strapped across her back is arguing at one of them.

pictured.coverAfter: She was tall and lean, and she had a great axe strapped across her back
pictured.outfit: sleeveless battered leather jerkin, knuckle wraps, dark trousers, scuffed boots, great axe Margery across her back, splinted forearm in a sling

event: She offers Elsie the half of her slate she has not used; the axe is Margery.

memory.fact: Tamsin fights with a great axe she calls Margery.
Tamsin Reyes is a Berserker of E-rank.

event: The Copper Hounds dropped Tamsin this morning, over the shield-bearer's arm.

memory.fact: This morning the Copper Hounds dropped Tamsin, after she broke their shield-bearer's arm.
This morning the Copper Hounds dropped Tamsin, after she broke their shield-bearer's arm.

event: Elsie's hand goes flat on Tamsin's wrist; Tamsin goes still, and her ears are red.
Elsie asks whether the arm is mending; Tamsin stares, and says probably.
A small woman in brass goggles, Ottilie Brandt called Tilly, comes out talking fast.

memory.fact: Tilly's blonde hair is in two long braids with singed ends, brass goggles pushed up on her head.

pictured.coverAfter: It was a small woman with brass goggles pushed up into her hair
pictured.outfit: cream blouse with rolled sleeves, too-big scorched apron, belt of corked vials

event: Thrown out of the Alchemists' College, she answers what she brews with three warnings.

memory.fact: The Alchemists' College threw Tilly out last week, after her brew blew out its east lab windows.
The Alchemists' College threw Tilly out last week, after her brew blew out its east lab windows.
Tilly talks fast, faster when nervous, and apologises before anything has gone wrong.
Tilly's father is a clockmaker on Gear Street who thinks she is still at the College.
Tilly's father is a clockmaker on Gear Street who thinks she is still at the College.

event: Tilly goes red to the ears when Elsie smiles, and drops her chalk twice.

memory.fact: Tilly Brandt is an Alchemist of F-rank.

event: Tamsin's guild notice: six lanterns for the apothecary, moonbells at the Glasswood.

memory.fact: On the F-rank board today: moonbells from the Glasswood's edge for an apothecary, six lanterns.

event: Elsie says the three could take it; Tamsin asks if she has been in a dungeon.

memory.fact: Elsie has never been inside a dungeon.

event: Elsie chalks three names on the last slate; Tilly writes hers under, then Tamsin.
Tilly asks her class; Elsie says Enthraller and does not look away.

memory.fact: Elsie Fairweather's class is Enthraller.

event: Tamsin says, so you can make me do anything; Elsie says that is not how hers works.

memory.fact: Elsie Fairweather's class is Enthraller.

event: Tilly asks about bonds; Cora watches the wrist, the chalk, the red ears, and writes nothing.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 15 (the wrist, the arm, the slate)
Bond: Tilly 10 (her red ears, the chalk)

event: Somebody brings bread and a jug, and the four of them eat standing at the board.
Tamsin says moonbells open at dusk, so they will go out at dusk tomorrow.

memory.fact: Moonbells open only between dusk and midnight, and a closed moonbell is worthless to an apothecary.

event: Elsie thinks the three of them are going to be friends, and is glad enough to hum.
The lamplighters' boats move along the canal, and the lanterns come on one by one.

memory.fact: Paper lanterns hang along every canal, and lamplighters' boats light them at dusk.

event: Cora opens the black ledger, writes nothing, and puts it back under her coat.
Asked what she will write, Cora says she has not decided.
Elsie says she will try to give her something good to write.
